[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The opening names God as wise and just with complete power and command, Allah as the unrivaled King, the All-Merciful as giving all creation the mercy of existence, and the Merciful as saving whom He wills in the afterlife.

[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The account is the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection; ḥisāb also means enumerating something and requiting it with good or evil.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The iftiʿāl form intensifies the nearness because no later community remains whose turn must first arrive.

[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | reports | Alternatively, account can mean recompense, making the verse a threat of events such as Badr and the Conquest, with people referring to Quraysh or all Arabs.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | On the primary reading, people means everyone generally, including the addressees and others.

[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#2/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their heedlessness is exposed when they are raised, or when events kill them and leave survivors humbled, so that they recognize truth and falsehood.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The surah's purpose is to prove the Hour's certainty and nearness, even through death, and the judgment of both eminent and lowly; the unique Creator cannot be prevented and does not alter his promise.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p63#s021/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The combined prophetic stories provide the proof: no single story independently establishes every aspect, but each points to part of it.

[ALUSI-FULL:v17p2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās, as cited by al-Razi, al-Qurṭubī, and al-Zamakhsharī, takes الناس to mean the polytheists, as the following verses describe them.
